status: Integrated M1 engineering experiment with synthetic food and assumed available water; not geographically validated habitability or historical prediction.

scope.localWindows: 120 km dated windows retained as controls; not the main dispersal domain

foodField: Synthetic spatially phased annual cosine renewal; equal annual potential across phases. Unique physical resource cells shared by all overlapping camp access areas. Not derived from climate or density. Reach is 7.5 km one-way along terrain-accessible segments. Net edible share is gross harvest / (1 + roundtrip terrain cost / 6 km); access expenditure is consumed in the ledger. Full untouched patches do not accrue fictitious renewal.
forecast: Fourteen-day accessible stock and renewal divided by competing demand; the focal private bag remains private. Perfect information accounts for incoming claims. Learned information uses resident observations, projected seasonal recovery, remembered competitors, and confidence exp(-age/90 days) toward a half-full unknown prior. Forecast error is recorded on arrival; the forecast is an approximation, not guaranteed food.

policies.food: Daily and arrival decisions consider physically reachable improving budgets; choose seeded coverage-weighted candidates above 0.1 improvement. Travel needs carried provisions. A feasible better destination can trigger 25% rationing/provision protection; unmet meals still increase condition deficit. Impossible journeys do not cause futile rationing.
policies.scheduled: Same resource, access, lifecycle and selected demographic response; original sampled mobility schedules. Under-provisioned journeys record deficits.

destinationQuadrature: Coverage-improvement sampling is weighted by represented land area (fixed-cell nearest-camp numerical quadrature). These weights correct uneven camp density; they neither allocate food ownership nor define foraging territories.
foragingSchedule: Daily harvest opportunity and arrival at a different camp; repeat decisions do not create extra harvest. Continuous intake and spoilage have an analytical solution, with condition exposure split at reserve exhaustion. Calendar boundaries have a 1e-9-day numerical tolerance.
condition: Exponential lag of unmet demand, bounded [0,1]. Quadratic excess hazard above threshold, integrated analytically, sampled as integer deaths monthly. Fertility multiplier is 1 minus annual mean lagged deficit. No scarcity reproduces the demographic reference. This response is an uncalibrated hypothesis, with explicit sensitivity alternatives.
controls: coupled=true enables response; coupled=false retains integrated movement and lifecycle but removes resource effects on mortality/fertility. ABI mode 0 remains the legacy experiment; mode 1 integrated coupled; mode 2 integrated uncoupled.
lifecycle: At annual census, healthy groups above 90 people with a year of residence may split; small co-residents below 20 may merge into groups up to 90. Limit 512 groups. Cohorts, food and accumulated person-time are conserved; children inherit knowledge without duplicating prior person-time.
occupation: Experimental establishment requires one year of continuous residence, deficit below 0.1 and annual accessible potential sufficient for demand. Current viable occupation is distinct from ever-established sites. Recolonization requires recorded vacancy and renewed sustained supported residence. Regional water is unknown, so this is not a real-world settlement viability claim.
boundaries: No group state reset at internal representation boundaries. Explicit sampled proposals outside the finite domain are counted and rejected; no wrapping, reflecting or teleportation. Domain-size sensitivity remains visible.
accounting: initial + replenished = environmental stock + carried + consumed + spoiled. Consumed includes separately reported foraging expenditure. Deficits are unmet dietary demand, not lost food. People = initial + births - deaths; scarcity deaths are a subset of deaths.
water: Unknown regionally; assumed available for engineering fixtures. No freshwater feasibility or reconstructed palaeohydrology.
limits: Synthetic food conversion, reach, access cost, season phase and condition parameters
Terrain-based static 100 ka sea-level scenario, not a validated local palaeoshoreline
No transient climate, boats, diet adaptation or historical arrival inference
Modern demographic and mobility references require ancient-transfer evaluation
No independent empirical validation of integrated dispersal
